paragraphs.text: And he called unto him his twelve disciples, and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of disease and all manner of sickness.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε ἐκβάλλειν αὐτὰ καὶ θεραπεύειν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai proskalesamenos tous dōdeka mathētas autou edōken autois exousian pneumatōn akathartōn hōste ekballein auta kai therapeuein pasan noson kai pasan malakian.

paragraphs.text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the [son] of Zebedee, and John his brother;
paragraphs.original: τῶν δὲ δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τὰ ὀνόματά ἐστιν ταῦτα· πρῶτος Σίμων ὁ λεγόμενος Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: tōn de dōdeka apostolōn ta onomata estin tauta· prōtos Simōn ho legomenos Petros kai Andreas ho adelphos autou, Iakōbos ho tou Zebedaiou kai Iōannēs ho adelphos autou,

paragraphs.text: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
paragraphs.original: Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος, Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης, Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖος,
paragraphs.translit: Philippos kai Bartholomaios, Thōmas kai Maththaios ho telōnēs, Iakōbos ho tou Halphaiou kai Thaddaios,

paragraphs.text: Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
paragraphs.original: Σίμων ὁ Καναναῖος καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης ὁ καὶ παραδοὺς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Simōn ho Kananaios kai Ioudas ho Iskariōtēs ho kai paradous auton.

paragraphs.text: These twelve Jesus sent forth, and charged them, saying, Go not into [any] way of the Gentiles, and enter not into any city of the Samaritans:
paragraphs.original: Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων· Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε·
paragraphs.translit: Toutous tous dōdeka apesteilen ho Iēsous parangeilas autois legōn· Eis hodon ethnōn mē apelthēte kai eis polin Samaritōn mē eiselthēte·

paragraphs.text: but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
paragraphs.original: πορεύεσθε δὲ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: poreuesthe de mallon pros ta probata ta apolōlota oikou Israēl.

paragraphs.text: And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.
paragraphs.original: πορευόμενοι δὲ κηρύσσετε λέγοντες ὅτι Ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: poreuomenoi de kēryssete legontes hoti Ēngiken hē basileia tōn ouranōn.

paragraphs.text: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons: freely ye received, freely give.
paragraphs.original: ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε, νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε, λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε, δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε· δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε.
paragraphs.translit: asthenountas therapeuete, nekrous egeirete, leprous katharizete, daimonia ekballete· dōrean elabete, dōrean dote.

paragraphs.text: Get you no gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses;
paragraphs.original: μὴ κτήσησθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκὸν εἰς τὰς ζώνας ὑμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: mē ktēsēsthe chryson mēde argyron mēde chalkon eis tas zōnas hymōn,

paragraphs.text: no wallet for [your] journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.
paragraphs.original: μὴ πήραν εἰς ὁδὸν μηδὲ δύο χιτῶνας μηδὲ ὑποδήματα μηδὲ ῥάβδον· ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: mē pēran eis hodon mēde dyo chitōnas mēde hypodēmata mēde rhabdon· axios gar ho ergatēs tēs trophēs autou.

paragraphs.text: And into whatsoever city or village ye shall enter, search out who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go forth.
paragraphs.original: εἰς ἣν δʼ ἂν πόλιν ἢ κώμην εἰσέλθητε, ἐξετάσατε τίς ἐν αὐτῇ ἄξιός ἐστιν· κἀκεῖ μείνατε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε.
paragraphs.translit: eis hēn dʼ an polin ē kōmēn eiselthēte, exetasate tis en autē axios estin· kakei meinate heōs an exelthēte.

paragraphs.text: And as ye enter into the house, salute it.
paragraphs.original: εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν·
paragraphs.translit: eiserchomenoi de eis tēn oikian aspasasthe autēn·

paragraphs.text: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ᾖ ἡ οἰκία ἀξία, ἐλθάτω ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ἐπʼ αὐτήν· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἀξία, ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιστραφήτω.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean men ē hē oikia axia, elthatō hē eirēnē hymōn epʼ autēn· ean de mē ē axia, hē eirēnē hymōn pros hymas epistraphētō.

paragraphs.text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, as ye go forth out of that house or that city, shake off the dust of your feet.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσῃ τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἐξερχόμενοι ἔξω τῆς οἰκίας ἢ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hos an mē dexētai hymas mēde akousē tous logous hymōn, exerchomenoi exō tēs oikias ē tēs poleōs ekeinēs ektinaxate ton koniorton tōn podōn hymōn.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment, than for that city.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται γῇ Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin, anektoteron estai gē Sodomōn kai Gomorrōn en hēmera kriseōs ē tē polei ekeinē.

paragraphs.text: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
paragraphs.original: Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς πρόβατα ἐν μέσῳ λύκων· γίνεσθε οὖν φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις καὶ ἀκέραιοι ὡς αἱ περιστεραί.
paragraphs.translit: Idou egō apostellō hymas hōs probata en mesō lykōn· ginesthe oun phronimoi hōs hoi opheis kai akeraioi hōs hai peristerai.

paragraphs.text: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to councils, and in theirs synagogues they will scourge you;
paragraphs.original: προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· παραδώσουσιν γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια, καὶ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν μαστιγώσουσιν ὑμᾶς·
paragraphs.translit: prosechete de apo tōn anthrōpōn· paradōsousin gar hymas eis synedria, kai en tais synagōgais autōn mastigōsousin hymas·

paragraphs.text: yea and before governors and kings shall ye be brought for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας δὲ καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai epi hēgemonas de kai basileis achthēsesthe heneken emou eis martyrion autois kai tois ethnesin.

paragraphs.text: But when they deliver you up, be not anxious how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that hour what ye shall speak.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν δὲ παραδῶσιν ὑμᾶς, μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί λαλήσητε· δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τί λαλήσητε·
paragraphs.translit: hotan de paradōsin hymas, mē merimnēsēte pōs ē ti lalēsēte· dothēsetai gar hymin en ekeinē tē hōra ti lalēsēte·

paragraphs.text: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar hymeis este hoi lalountes alla to pneuma tou patros hymōn to laloun en hymin.

paragraphs.text: And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his child: and children shall rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
paragraphs.original: παραδώσει δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον, καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: paradōsei de adelphos adelphon eis thanaton kai patēr teknon, kai epanastēsontai tekna epi goneis kai thanatōsousin autous.

paragraphs.text: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name`s sake: but he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου· ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai esesthe misoumenoi hypo pantōn dia to onoma mou· ho de hypomeinas eis telos houtos sōthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone through the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν δὲ διώκωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ, φεύγετε εἰς τὴν ἑτέραν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ τελέσητε τὰς πόλεις τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: hotan de diōkōsin hymas en tē polei tautē, pheugete eis tēn heteran· amēn gar legō hymin, ou mē telesēte tas poleis tou Israēl heōs an elthē ho hyios tou anthrōpou.

paragraphs.text: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.
paragraphs.original: Οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον οὐδὲ δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Ouk estin mathētēs hyper ton didaskalon oude doulos hyper ton kyrion autou.

paragraphs.text: It is enough for the disciple that he be as his teacher, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more them of his household!
paragraphs.original: ἀρκετὸν τῷ μαθητῇ ἵνα γένηται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ δοῦλος ὡς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ. εἰ τὸν οἰκοδεσπότην Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐπεκάλεσαν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τοὺς οἰκιακοὺς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: arketon tō mathētē hina genētai hōs ho didaskalos autou, kai ho doulos hōs ho kyrios autou. ei ton oikodespotēn Beelzeboul epekalesan, posō mallon tous oikiakous autou.

paragraphs.text: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.
paragraphs.original: Μὴ οὖν φοβηθῆτε αὐτούς· οὐδὲν γάρ ἐστιν κεκαλυμμένον ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: Mē oun phobēthēte autous· ouden gar estin kekalymmenon ho ouk apokalyphthēsetai, kai krypton ho ou gnōsthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: What I tell you in the darkness, speak ye in the light; and what ye hear in the ear, proclaim upon the house-tops.
paragraphs.original: ὃ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτί· καὶ ὃ εἰς τὸ οὖς ἀκούετε, κηρύξατε ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.
paragraphs.translit: ho legō hymin en tē skotia, eipate en tō phōti· kai ho eis to ous akouete, kēryxate epi tōn dōmatōn.

paragraphs.text: And be not afraid of them that kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεννόντων τὸ σῶμα τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν μὴ δυναμένων ἀποκτεῖναι· φοβεῖσθε δὲ μᾶλλον τὸν δυνάμενον καὶ ψυχὴν καὶ σῶμα ἀπολέσαι ἐν γεέννῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai mē phobeisthe apo tōn apoktennontōn to sōma tēn de psychēn mē dynamenōn apokteinai· phobeisthe de mallon ton dynamenon kai psychēn kai sōma apolesai en geennē.

paragraphs.text: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? and not one of them shall fall on the ground without your Father:
paragraphs.original: οὐχὶ δύο στρουθία ἀσσαρίου πωλεῖται; καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐ πεσεῖται ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ouchi dyo strouthia assariou pōleitai; kai hen ex autōn ou peseitai epi tēn gēn aneu tou patros hymōn.

paragraphs.text: but the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
paragraphs.original: ὑμῶν δὲ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς πᾶσαι ἠριθμημέναι εἰσίν.
paragraphs.translit: hymōn de kai hai triches tēs kephalēs pasai ērithmēmenai eisin.

paragraphs.text: Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.
paragraphs.original: μὴ οὖν φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε ὑμεῖς.
paragraphs.translit: mē oun phobeisthe· pollōn strouthiōn diapherete hymeis.

paragraphs.text: Every one therefore who shall confess me before men, him will I also confess before my Father who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁμολογήσω κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: Pas oun hostis homologēsei en emoi emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn, homologēsō kagō en autō emprosthen tou patros mou tou en ouranois·

paragraphs.text: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: ὅστις δʼ ἂν ἀρνήσηταί με ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἀρνήσομαι κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: hostis dʼ an arnēsētai me emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn, arnēsomai kagō auton emprosthen tou patros mou tou en ouranois.

paragraphs.text: Think not that I came to send peace on the earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.
paragraphs.original: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν· οὐκ ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἀλλὰ μάχαιραν.
paragraphs.translit: Mē nomisēte hoti ēlthon balein eirēnēn epi tēn gēn· ouk ēlthon balein eirēnēn alla machairan.

paragraphs.text: For I came to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law:
paragraphs.original: ἦλθον γὰρ διχάσαι ἄνθρωπον κατὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ θυγατέρα κατὰ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφην κατὰ τῆς πενθερᾶς αὐτῆς,
paragraphs.translit: ēlthon gar dichasai anthrōpon kata tou patros autou kai thygatera kata tēs mētros autēs kai nymphēn kata tēs pentheras autēs,

paragraphs.text: and a man`s foes [shall be] they of his own household.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οἱ οἰκιακοὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai echthroi tou anthrōpou hoi oikiakoi autou.

paragraphs.text: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
paragraphs.original: ὁ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος· καὶ ὁ φιλῶν υἱὸν ἢ θυγατέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος·
paragraphs.translit: ho philōn patera ē mētera hyper eme ouk estin mou axios· kai ho philōn hyion ē thygatera hyper eme ouk estin mou axios·

paragraphs.text: And he that doth not take his cross and follow after me, is not worthy of me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃς οὐ λαμβάνει τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ ὀπίσω μου, οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος.
paragraphs.translit: kai hos ou lambanei ton stauron autou kai akolouthei opisō mou, ouk estin mou axios.

paragraphs.text: He that findeth his life shall lose it; and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.
paragraphs.original: ὁ εὑρὼν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ ἀπολέσας τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: ho heurōn tēn psychēn autou apolesei autēn, kai ho apolesas tēn psychēn autou heneken emou heurēsei autēn.

paragraphs.text: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ δεχόμενος ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὁ ἐμὲ δεχόμενος δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
paragraphs.translit: Ho dechomenos hymas eme dechetai, kai ho eme dechomenos dechetai ton aposteilanta me.

paragraphs.text: He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet`s reward: and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man`s reward.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δεχόμενος προφήτην εἰς ὄνομα προφήτου μισθὸν προφήτου λήμψεται, καὶ ὁ δεχόμενος δίκαιον εἰς ὄνομα δικαίου μισθὸν δικαίου λήμψεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho dechomenos prophētēn eis onoma prophētou misthon prophētou lēmpsetai, kai ho dechomenos dikaion eis onoma dikaiou misthon dikaiou lēmpsetai.

paragraphs.text: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only, in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you he shall in no wise lose his reward.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν ποτίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ποτήριον ψυχροῦ μόνον εἰς ὄνομα μαθητοῦ, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai hos an potisē hena tōn mikrōn toutōn potērion psychrou monon eis onoma mathētou, amēn legō hymin, ou mē apolesē ton misthon autou.
